bias.headline: Conditions are moderately bearish (led by Market Structure) — on thin evidence, so treat the description itself as tentative. This describes the current state, not a prediction.

topBearish.label: Market Structure
evidenceFor: Last swing high rejected; no reclaim above 766.81
topBearish.confidenceBasis: 12 swing highs and 12 swing lows over 120 sessions. Confidence scales with how decisively both legs moved relative to the 9% range, and is capped at 75 because a two-pivot sequence is short.
topBearish.explanation: SPY is printing lower highs and lower lows — an intact downtrend. Last swing high 759.81 vs prior 766.81; last swing low 733.00 vs prior 759.97.
topBearish.whyItMatters: Structure is the only read that describes the SHAPE of a move rather than its size. Two markets up the same amount are different trades if one is making higher lows and the other keeps undercutting them — and structure is what a stop is placed against.
topBearish.nextTrigger: breaks up above the last swing high of 759.81

topBearish.label: Market Breadth
topBearish.confidenceBasis: 82 individual companies, each counted once, against 500 sessions of this panel's own breadth history. A participation count rather than an index proxy — but still a large-cap panel, not a full advance/decline line, so confidence is capped at 75.
topBearish.explanation: 43% of 82 companies are trading above their own 50-session average. That is unusually narrow — higher than only 25% of its own past readings for this group, whose typical session reads 57%.
topBearish.whyItMatters: A rally carried by one or two names is fragile in a way the index level does not show. Broad participation is what separates a durable advance from a narrow one.
topBearish.nextTrigger: stops being bearish if it climbs out of the bottom third of its own past readings — right now it is higher than only 25% of them

topBearish.label: Volatility
topBearish.confidenceBasis: 499 prior sessions of this instrument's own ATR history. Confidence is halved deliberately: the volatility-return relationship is a conditional regularity, not a mechanism.
topBearish.explanation: SPY typically moves 1.71% in a day right now — more volatile than 91% of its own past. That is elevated volatility, and stocks tend to get more violent on the way down than on the way up.
topBearish.whyItMatters: Position size and stop distance both scale with volatility, so the same trade is a different risk in a different regime. In equities specifically, expanding volatility tends to accompany falling prices.
topBearish.nextTrigger: stops being bullish if it falls out of the top third of its own past readings — right now it is higher than 91% of them

watchNext.label: Trend Strength
watchNext.confidenceBasis: Path efficiency of 0.15 over 60 sessions — the distance actually covered divided by the total ground travelled to cover it (Kaufman's efficiency ratio). Confidence rises with efficiency and reaches 100 at 0.60, a strongly directional path.
watchNext.explanation: Over 60 sessions SPY moved -6.3%, and only 15% of its day-to-day movement went toward getting there — the rest was back and forth. That is a round trip rather than a trend, so no direction is claimed from it.

conflicts: Net move is negative but the path is inefficient — the sign is not evidence of a trend.
watchNext.nextTrigger: only takes a side once the path gets cleaner — 0.20 of the moves in one direction rather than back and forth, against 0.15 now
